sections.h2: What do Meeker County, MN sellers need to know about property tax?
sections.html:
In Meeker County the Auditor builds the tax bill, the Treasurer collects it, and the Assessor decides the value and class it is based on. All three offices share the Meeker County Government Center at 114 N Holcombe Avenue in Litchfield, so a seller can sort out most questions in one trip.

State statute sets the dates. Half of the bill is due before May 16 and the other half before October 16, and the Treasurer's office says penalty rates for late payment also come from state law. Before you list, confirm that the current half is paid and ask what, if anything, is still owed from earlier years.

  • Treasurer, Suite 100: 320-693-5345, open Monday to Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Auditor, Suite 150: 320-693-5212, for parcel records, tax rates and special assessments.
  • Assessor: 320-693-5205, for homestead applications and value questions.

sections.h2: Where is Meeker County and what are its homes like?
sections.html:
Meeker County lies in west central Minnesota between Stearns County to the north and McLeod County to the southeast. It spans 645 square miles, of which 608 are land and 37 are water. The territorial legislature created it on February 23, 1856, and named it for Bradley B. Meeker, a territorial judge. The county seat moved from Forest City to Litchfield in 1869, after a railroad spur arrived there. Cities include Litchfield, Dassel, Darwin, Cosmos, Cedar Mills, Grove City, Kingston and Watkins, plus part of Eden Valley. Low hills, ponds and lakes make up most of the terrain, and Greenleaf Lake State Recreation Area lies within the county.

The 2020 census recorded 23,400 residents and the Census Bureau estimates 23,603 for 2025. In 2020, 71.9% of residents lived in rural areas, and 12.4% of the 10,576 housing units were vacant. QuickFacts shows 10,969 housing units in 2025, a 79.3% owner-occupied rate, a $249,000 median owner-occupied home value for 2020 to 2024, and a median household income of $75,446. Builders pulled 48 building permits in 2025. Median gross rent is $904.

sections.h2: How is a Meeker County tax bill built?
sections.html:
The Auditor's office calculates tax capacity rates and then computes tax on roughly 18,000 parcels covering real property, personal property and mobile homes. The totals reflect the budgets of the county, townships, cities, school districts and special taxing districts. Special assessments certified by the county, townships and cities are added to the matching parcel and passed through on the same statement.

Ditch systems are a Meeker County detail that sellers of farmland and rural lots should ask about. The same office keeps the financial records for each county and joint drainage system and files assessments for maintenance costs. After the money comes in, the Treasurer distributes it to the townships, cities, school districts and special districts.

Statements usually mail in late March. Truth in Taxation notices, which estimate the next year's tax, mail in November. Taxes left unpaid for three or more years are subject to forfeiture.

sections.h2: What does a late payment cost in Meeker County?
sections.html:
The schedule comes from Minnesota Statutes 279.01 and applies in every county, including Meeker. Homestead property pays the lower rates, and nonhomestead property pays double.

Late payment penalty on an unpaid half, from Minnesota Statutes 279.01
WhenHomesteadNonhomestead
Unpaid on the due date2%4%
Still unpaid on the first of the next month2% more4% more
Each later month through December1% more1% more
Ceiling8%12%

The statute shifts the first due date to 21 days after the postmark if the statement was mailed after April 25, and a bill of $100 or less is due in a single payment on the first date. Farm homesteads and other qualifying agricultural land owe no penalty on the second half if it is paid by November 15. The treasurer can accept more or less than the exact installment, and a partial payment goes to the oldest unpaid installment first.

sections.h2: How can I pay Meeker County property tax?
sections.html:
The Treasurer lists four routes. Choose one that fits the closing calendar.

  • By mail to the Meeker County Treasurer at 114 N Holcombe Avenue, Suite 100, Litchfield, MN 55355. The envelope must be postmarked on or before the due date. Pre-addressed envelopes come with the statement for owners without escrow.
  • In person with cash, check or card at the Government Center. The Treasurer's office is the first one on the right inside the main doors.
  • By credit card, which adds 2.5% to the total, or by e-check, which costs a flat $1.50 up to $10,000 and $10 above that.
  • By direct debit from a checking or savings account. Download the authorization form, mail it in, or call 320-693-5345 and ask for the materials.

If a mortgage company escrows your tax, the Treasurer sends the payment information to that lender, and the lender pays by the due date.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Meeker County valuation?
sections.html:
Start with the assessor, then work upward. The statutory path has three stages, and each one limits the next.

First comes the local board of appeal and equalization, which is the town board or city council. It meets between April 1 and May 31 and has 20 days to finish. A local board can lower individual assessments, yet total cuts may not reduce the assessor's overall value by more than one percent, and it cannot grant an exemption. Second is the county board, made up of the commissioners and the auditor. It may raise or lower a parcel to what it believes is market value, but it must first give notice and set a hearing before it raises one.

The last stage is a petition to district court or the Tax Court, which has to be filed by April 30 of the year the tax is payable. A later notice changes that clock: if the owner is first told of a new value, class or exemption change after February 28 of the payable year, the owner has 60 days from the mailing date to start the appeal. A board cannot grant an individual reduction to an owner who has refused the assessor access to inspect the property.

sections.h2: How do homestead and refund rules affect a Meeker County sale?
sections.html:
Homestead status sets the penalty rate, and it depends on who lives in the home. Meeker County tells new owners to apply as soon as they move in. The owner must buy and occupy the home by December 1, and the application must reach the assessor by December 15 to count for the next year's taxes. State law requires Social Security numbers and signatures for every owner who lives in the home and for spouses not on the deed. Owners cannot claim more than one homestead, and an approved homestead does not need to be refiled unless the assessor asks.

A seller must tell the assessor within 30 days of a sale or a change of primary residence. If not, the property may be taxed at its correct class plus a penalty of the same amount. Separately, the Minnesota Department of Revenue runs a property tax refund based on household income and taxes paid on a principal residence. Meeker County sends refund questions to the state.

sections.h2: What should a Meeker County seller check at closing?
sections.html:
Three state rules shape the paperwork. Under 272.12 the auditor must certify no delinquent taxes before a deed is recorded, and the deed carries the note "no delinquent taxes and transfer entered." A certificate of value goes to the auditor for any sale above $3,000 under 272.115, and the grantor, buyer or an agent may file it. A deed that conveys only part of a parcel also needs the treasurer's certification that the current year's tax on the whole parcel is paid, under 272.121.

Ask the Auditor about any ditch assessment on a rural parcel, and ask the Treasurer for the payoff figure for the current half. A buyer's lender will want both numbers before it funds.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Meeker County?
faqs.a: Pay the Meeker County Treasurer in person, by mail, by card or e-check, or by direct debit. The office is at 114 N Holcombe Avenue, Suite 100, Litchfield, and the phone number is 320-693-5345.

faqs.q: How much is the credit card fee on Meeker County taxes?
faqs.a: It is 2.5% of the total. E-checks carry a flat $1.50 fee for payments up to $10,000 and $10 for larger ones.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Meeker County taxes late?
faqs.a: Homestead property is charged 2% on the due date and 2% more on the first of the next month, then 1% each month through December, up to 8%. Nonhomestead starts at 4%, adds 4%, then 1% a month up to 12%.

faqs.q: When must I apply for homestead in Meeker County?
faqs.a: Apply by December 15, and only if you bought and moved in by December 1. That sets the classification for taxes payable the following year.

faqs.q: How long can taxes go unpaid in Meeker County before forfeiture?
faqs.a: The Auditor's office says taxes left unpaid for three or more years are subject to forfeiture. Contact the Treasurer well before then to learn the payoff amount.
